content:
jess: Quick check — I'm about to merge a small TF change that reorders route table associations for the analytics subnets. Not changing CIDRs, just assoc priority to prefer the zonal NATs. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/4822 :eyes:

matt: Pinged the PR. Can you paste the plan here? Want to confirm no implicit route deletions.

jess: Plan excerpt below — it's only association order, Terraform shows a replace on aws_route_table_association analytics->private-rt because of computed position change. This should be safe (non-disruptive):

```
-/+ aws_route_table_association.analytics_subnet_a (new resource required)
      id: "rtbassoc-0a1b2c3" => <computed>
      route_table_id: "rtb-xyz" => "rtb-xyz"
      subnet_id: "subnet-aaa" => "subnet-aaa"
```

jess: The trick is we have an ordering-sensitive module that sets a list so Terraform decides to recreate the association instead of just reassigning. I tested in staging and the subnet stayed in-place, no traffic drop.

kai: Staging smoke looked fine for pods and egress, right? Any kube-proxy or node scheduling flaps observed?

jess: Staging: brief ARP churn on the NAT ENI for ~10s, no conntrack issues, existing TCP sessions (ssh, postgres) persisted. App pods didn't restart.

matt: Ok. Two asks before merge: 1) add an upgrade note in the PR description mentioning transient ARP churn, 2) tag the affected subnets with `networking:canary` so our reconciler picks the subset for canary rollout.

jess: Will add both. For tagging, I'm planning to run a quick one-off to add tag via Terraform change rather than manual tag. Snippet: 

```
resource "aws_subnet" "analytics_a" {
  # existing attrs...
  tags = merge(var.common_tags, { "networking:canary" = "true" })
}
```

matt: Good. Also confirm the route priority for private RTs — we want the nat-route to have precedence over the privatelink route for outbound to S3. If reorder flips that, might break uploads.

jess: I've checked: we only change association order, route table contents remain identical. The S3 privatelink route is a more specific prefix (s3 endpoints use prefix lists), so no conflict expected.

dave: Just to flag: when associations recreate, association IDs change and our tagging script that looks up association by ID will need to tolerate new IDs. I can update the script to fallback to subnet->route_table lookup.

infra-bot: automated-check: terraform plan for branch jess/reorder-assoc -> 1 change (aws_route_table_association replacement). No drifting resources. CI: unit-tests ok.

matt: Sweet. If you add the PR note and the subnet tag change, I'll approve and merge during the 11:00 window (low traffic). Can you schedule the canary and watch egress metrics?

jess: Yep. I'll merge at 11:00, then tag `networking:canary=true` via TF apply in the same commit. I'll monitor NAT bytes, error rates, and S3 PUT latency for 30m. Will post back here with live numbers. :thumbsup:

kai: If anything spikes, flip the tag off and rollback the association change? Do we have rollback doc for this?

matt: Rollback plan: revert the PR and apply. Because association recreation is the change, revert will recreate the previous assoc — should converge back. Follow runbook: https://wiki.redwood.ai/runbooks/vpc-assoc-rollback

jess: Noted. I'll paste canary metrics here after apply. Thanks all.
